entry.idea: Computer chips are running into limits set by the materials they are made from, so Discovered Materials uses AI to search for and test new materials that could replace them, starting with materials that pull heat out of stacked 3D chips.
entry.lesson: When a whole industry is stuck behind one stubborn physical limit, using AI to search a huge space of untried options can turn a research problem into a company.
entry.name: Discovered Materials

growth.basis: substitute: quality of seed investors (Y Combinator, Lightspeed India Partners, Peak XV Partners)
growth.reason: There are no user or revenue numbers yet, but the seed round drew top investors including Y Combinator, Lightspeed India, and Peak XV Partners.

market.reason: New materials for chip heat management could be needed across the whole worldwide semiconductor and AI-chip industry.

tech.reason: Discovering and owning IP on genuinely new materials is hard to copy quickly, though the approach is new and unproven at scale.

entry.twist: It wants to own the intellectual property on the new materials it finds with AI, sitting as a new business layer between materials research and chipmakers rather than just publishing papers.
entry.who_pays: Chipmakers and chip-packaging companies would license or buy the materials it discovers.
entry.why_now: Chipmakers are pushing against the physical limits of today's materials right as AI has become good enough to search through far more untested material options than people could test by hand.
